item.title: Strategy (MSTR) is to be removed from MSCI Global Investable Market Indexes following MSCI's implementation of a new non-operating company rule.
item.description:
The immediate trade is the November 30 close, when index trackers have to sell. That event is well flagged and partly priced, so the reaction in the stock may come before the date rather than on it. The wider read-through is for crypto treasury companies. Metaplanet in Japan was in the same simulated deletion bucket, and SharpLink is on the watch list, so their status is worth checking as the full list circulates. For bitcoin, the concern is slower buying. Strategy has been one of the steadiest corporate buyers, and a thinner passive shareholder base could raise the cost of the equity it issues to fund purchases. If other index providers follow MSCI’s lead, that pressure would grow.

---

This is the big news right now ICYMI:

  • Nvidia stock plunges after hours as New York Times reports new Jensen Huang relationship allegation
  • Nvidia CEO Huang faces 2nd relationship report as NYT links him to senior executive

---

MSCI has decided Strategy looks more like a bitcoin fund than a software company, and index trackers now have until November 30 to sell.

Summary:

  • MSCI will remove Strategy from its global indexes, including the MSCI USA Index, effective after the close on November 30
  • The decision is the first under MSCI’s new non-operating company rule, which screens operating assets and five financial ratios
  • Strategy went straight onto the deletion list, meaning it had already failed the two-year buffer for existing index members
  • Analysts estimated about $2.8 billion of passive selling, although that was calculated for MSCI’s earlier proposal
  • Strategy says trackers hold about 13 million shares, or 3.1% of its basic shares, and Saylor calls the rule discriminatory
  • Shares fell 0.8% after hours on Wednesday and are down about 20% this year

Strategy, the largest corporate holder of bitcoin, will be removed from MSCI’s global indexes after the index provider ruled that it more closely resembles an investment fund than an operating business. MSCI confirmed the deletion in its November index review on Wednesday. It takes effect after the close on November 30 and includes the flagship MSCI USA Index, according to Reuters and the published review list.

This is the first review under MSCI’s new non-operating company rule, which was finalised in mid-October. The rule first looks at a company’s operating assets and then tests it against five financial ratios. Companies that fail at least four of the five can be ruled ineligible. Existing index members generally have to fail across two annual reporting periods before they are removed. Strategy went straight onto the deletion list rather than the watch list, which means it had already used up that buffer.

The decision ends a reprieve that has lasted all year. In January, MSCI held back from excluding crypto treasury companies and promised a wider review of businesses whose main activity is holding assets. That review produced a deliberately asset-neutral test in August, but Strategy still failed it. A simulation using May data flagged Strategy, Japan’s Metaplanet and uranium holder Yellow Cake as deletions.

In practice, the removal forces selling by funds that track MSCI benchmarks. Analysts have estimated that selling at around $2.8 billion, although the figure was calculated for MSCI’s earlier crypto-specific proposal. Strategy has argued the impact will be modest. It says index trackers hold about 13 million shares, roughly 3.1% of its basic shares outstanding and less than a day’s typical trading volume. Executive chairman Michael Saylor has called the rule discriminatory and argues Strategy runs a genuine software business.

Strategy shares fell 0.8% in extended trading on Wednesday and are down about 20% this year, while bitcoin has lost about 15%. The bigger question is the longer term. Strategy funds its bitcoin buying largely by issuing shares, and losing part of its passive shareholder base could make that model more expensive, particularly if other index providers adopt similar rules.

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: Nvidia stock plunges after hours as New York Times reports new Jensen Huang relationship allegation
item.description:
WOW

"NVIDIA PREPARING TO OUST NVIDIA CEO JENSEN HUANG": WSJ

NVDA shares reverse Wednesday's gains following a report that Nvidia's CEO had a relationship with an executive reporting to him. If confirmed, the allegations could add a new corporate-governance problem to the company's existing leadership controversy.

Nvidia (NVDA) shares are falling sharply in after-hours trading following a new report from The New York Times alleging that CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with a company executive who reports to him.

According to a market quote captured at 00:11 GMT+2 on November 12, NVDA traded at $167.37 after hours, down $6.36 or 3.66% from Wednesday's regular-session close of $173.73.

The decline reverses more than Wednesday's 2.87% regular-session gain.

Why the latest Nvidia allegations matter to investors

The New York Times reported the new allegation late Wednesday, adding another potential complication for Nvidia's board of directors.

The company is already investigating Huang following earlier reports concerning his relationship with a Chinese businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence reportedly identified as having connections to Chinese intelligence.

That earlier controversy raised questions about national security, corporate oversight and whether sensitive information could have been compromised.

The latest allegation, however, introduces a potentially different concern.

If Huang had a relationship with an executive who reported directly to him, investors could reasonably question whether there were conflicts of interest involving management decisions, compensation, promotions or internal corporate governance.

A personal relationship does not, by itself, establish wrongdoing or improper conduct. The significance depends on the circumstances, the company's policies, what was disclosed to the board and whether any business decisions were affected.

The new allegation has not been independently verified by investingLive.

Why Nvidia stock could face additional pressure

Jensen Huang is not an ordinary corporate CEO. He co-founded Nvidia and has been central to its transformation into one of the world's most important artificial intelligence companies.

For shareholders, the concern is not simply the executive's personal conduct. It is whether repeated controversies could undermine confidence in Nvidia's leadership, distract management or increase pressure on its board.

There are three particularly important implications.

Corporate governance: Investors may demand clearer answers about how Nvidia's board oversees its CEO and manages potential conflicts of interest.

Leadership continuity: Any widening of the investigation could raise further questions about succession planning at a company closely associated with its founder.

Valuation and investor confidence: Even without changes to Nvidia's chip demand, earnings or competitive position, greater uncertainty about leadership could influence how much investors are willing to pay for the stock.

That does not mean Huang will leave Nvidia or that the allegations will ultimately affect the company's operations.

But investors may increasingly distinguish between confidence in Nvidia's AI business and confidence in its corporate leadership.

What NVDA traders should watch next

The immediate question is whether the after-hours selling continues when regular U.S. trading resumes Thursday, November 12.

The reported decline comes while the Nasdaq futures market is closed, limiting the ability to draw conclusions about the broader technology sector's reaction at that moment.

Traders should monitor whether Nvidia underperforms the Nasdaq and semiconductor stocks once futures trading resumes, and whether the company or its board responds to the latest reporting.

A recovery toward Wednesday's $173.73 closing price would suggest the initial selling is being absorbed. Sustained weakness would raise the possibility that investors are assigning a greater risk premium to Nvidia's leadership uncertainty.

For now, the market is reacting to another allegation rather than a confirmed finding of misconduct. What matters next is the evidence, the board's response and whether the situation begins to affect the company's ability to operate under its existing leadership.

This article was written by Itai Levitan at investinglive.com.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Huang faces 2nd relationship report as NYT links him to senior executive
item.description:
This shifts the Huang story from a national security question toward a corporate governance one, which is easier for investors to price and harder for the board to dismiss. A relationship with a direct report raises code-of-conduct issues, and it widens what the board’s investigation may need to examine. Huang is closely identified with Nvidia’s strategy and customer relationships, so any hint of leadership change would be a material risk for the stock. Because Nvidia is one of the S&P 500’s biggest weights, that risk reaches broad index exposure too. Expect the board review to compete with guidance for attention in next week’s results call, and headline-driven volatility around the November 17 results and the November 18 House briefing.

---

This is just turning into gossip magazine fodder now. Anyway, this is probably the final nail in Huang's coffin. 

Earlier:

  • Lutnick stalls Trump’s third Nvidia chip diversion crackdown this year, Axios says
  • Three risks for Nvidia shares after Huang admits affair with suspected Chinese spy

---

The Huang story is no longer only about China, and a relationship with a direct report puts Nvidia’s own code of conduct at the centre of the board’s review.

Summary:

  • The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s VP of health care, who reports to him, citing five people who worked at the company
  • Nvidia’s code of conduct tells staff to avoid conflicts, including personal relationships, and says it promptly investigates misconduct
  • The board is already investigating Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, whom US officials identified as a Chinese intelligence asset, with Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz leading the review
  • China denies the espionage claims, and Nvidia has said earlier allegations about Megaspeed diverting chips were debunked
  • Three House committee chairs have requested a closed-door briefing with Huang, reportedly on November 18
  • Nvidia reports third-quarter results on November 17

Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of health care, who reports to him, The New York Times reported, citing five people who worked at the company. The relationship had not been reported before. It widens the scrutiny facing the head of the world’s leading AI chipmaker, less than a week before Nvidia reports quarterly results.

The report matters as a governance issue, not only a personal one. Nvidia’s code of conduct tells employees to avoid situations that create conflicts, including personal relationships, and says the company promptly investigates reports of misconduct. Many large companies bar managers from relationships with subordinates, because such ties can raise questions about pay, promotion and oversight. Both Huang and Powell are married to other people, according to the Times.

The new claim adds to an investigation already under way. Last month, the Times reported that US officials had identified Alice Huang as a Chinese intelligence asset. She is an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center company, and had become close to the Nvidia CEO. She is no relation to Jensen Huang. After he acknowledged an affair with her, Nvidia’s board opened an investigation this month, led by the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz. The board has said it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised. China has denied the espionage claims, and Alice Huang has not responded to requests for comment.

Nvidia has also pushed back on the wider allegations. It said earlier claims that Megaspeed diverted chips had been investigated and debunked last year, and Jensen Huang has described the company’s dealings with Megaspeed as normal.

Pressure is building in Washington too. The Republican chairs of three House committees have asked Huang to attend a closed-door briefing on his dealings with Alice Huang, reportedly on November 18. That is the day after Nvidia’s third-quarter results on November 17, when investors will be listening for any comment on the board’s review alongside the numbers. Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and built it into the premier supplier of AI chips, which makes the question of how much the company depends on him an unusually sharp one for shareholders. 

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: Lutnick stalls Trump’s third Nvidia chip diversion crackdown this year, Axios says
item.description:
For Nvidia, this adds another layer of policy uncertainty to a week already dominated by its board’s probe, and it keeps China-linked headline risk high heading into the requested House briefing. If enforcement tightens, it could weigh on sales routed through third-country buyers in Southeast Asia, although sales made through those channels are hard to size from public data. Nvidia is one of the heaviest weights in the S&P 500, so stock-specific shocks can move the wider index even when most other stocks are rising. Wall Street rebounded on Monday after the prior week’s selloff in AI stocks, but Nvidia fell, a sign that its own risks are now partly separate from the wider AI trade. A visible split between Bessent and Lutnick also matters beyond chips, because it raises questions about how consistently trade and export policy toward China will be applied.

---

Earlier:

  • Mizuho’s Klein calls Nvidia ‘silly cheap’ below 10x earnings despite Huang uncertainty
  • Morgans’ Stickley: S&P 500 up after every midterm since 1950 as Nvidia looks cheap

---

The White House wants to crack down on Nvidia chips leaking into China, but the department meant to enforce it is reportedly the one holding things up.

Summary:

  • Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has repeatedly stalled a crackdown on companies suspected of diverting Nvidia chips to China, Axios reported, citing high-level sources
  • Trump authorized the crackdown last Thursday, the third time this year, after consulting Elon Musk
  • In a Situation Room meeting with Bessent, Hegseth, Greer and Rubio, Bessent confronted Lutnick over his department’s resistance to enforcing the controls
  • Lutnick appeared to agree but said he needed to check with Trump, the report said
  • The report comes days after Nvidia’s board opened an independent probe into reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort

US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has repeatedly held up President Donald Trump’s crackdown on companies suspected of diverting Nvidia’s AI chips to China, Axios reported on Wednesday, citing high-level sources. The report reveals a split inside the administration over how hard to enforce export controls. It also comes while Nvidia is already facing heavy China-related scrutiny of its own.

According to Axios, Trump authorized the crackdown last Thursday after consulting Elon Musk. It was the third time this year he has done so. The same day, Lutnick met in the Situation Room with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Bessent challenged Lutnick over his department’s resistance to carrying out the controls. Lutnick appeared to agree but said he needed to check with Trump first, the report said.

Lutnick’s role matters because enforcement sits with the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security, which licenses chip exports and polices diversion. A delay at Commerce can slow enforcement even after the White House has signed off. Diversion usually happens through buyers in third countries, often in Southeast Asian hubs such as Singapore, who resell restricted chips into China. In June, the bureau moved to close a loophole that may have let overseas units of Chinese companies obtain top-end Nvidia processors, according to Reuters.

The timing is awkward for Nvidia. On November 8, its board opened an independent investigation after reports that chief executive Jensen Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. Independent directors are leading it, with help from outside counsel. The board said it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised, and that it still has confidence in Huang. The New York Times reported that Megaspeed, a Singapore-based firm, bought about $4.8 billion of Nvidia chips over two years, although no wrongdoing by the company has been established. Nvidia shares fell about 4% on November 9, the first trading session after the board’s announcement.

Three Republican House committee chairs have reportedly asked for a closed-door briefing with Huang on November 18. For investors, the question is whether the Lutnick dispute ends in tougher, faster enforcement or a quieter compromise. Either way, Washington is now testing Nvidia’s China exposure from several directions at once.

Ahead:

  • Nvidia reports on Tuesday, 17 November, after the US close.
  • Nvidia will host a conference call on Tuesday, November 17, at 2 p.m. PT (5 p.m. ET) to discuss its financial results for the third quarter of fiscal year 2027, which ended October 25, 2026. That’s 22:00 GMT. Ahead of the call, Nvidia will provide written commentary from the CFO.

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: Anthropic IPO oversubscribed several times ahead of record $90 billion listing
item.description:
Raising close to $90 billion takes a lot of cash, and some fund managers may trim existing megacap tech holdings to make room, which could weigh on the Nasdaq as pricing approaches. Heavy oversubscription is a positive read-through for AI infrastructure stocks, especially the seven companies in the placement, because it shows public appetite for direct AI exposure remains strong. A strong first day would likely support the wider IPO pipeline, including OpenAI, which is reportedly aiming for 2027. A weak open would hit sentiment across AI-linked equities.

---

Earlier:

  • US stocks rally as AI shares rebound
  • Anthropic reserves up to 20% of its $64 billion IPO for retail investors

---

Anthropic is heading into its debut with orders well ahead of supply, but the record-breaking $90 billion headline depends on pricing at the very top of the range.

Summary:

  • Anthropic’s IPO is already oversubscribed several times, driven by anchor-sized indications of interest, Bloomberg reported, citing unnamed sources
  • Shares are marketed at $70 to $78 each, implying a valuation of about $1.4 trillion, with trading expected to start next Thursday
  • The company is offering around 801 million Class A shares, and existing investors are selling roughly 24 million more
  • AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC have committed to buy $26 billion of Class N stock in a private placement
  • The combined target of about $90 billion would top SpaceX’s June record of about $86 billion including its over-allotment
  • CEO Dario Amodei will hold a live-streamed event with JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon on Friday

Anthropic’s initial public offering is already covered several times over, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter. That puts the Claude developer on course for what could be the largest stock market debut on record when its shares start trading next Thursday. The listing would make Anthropic the first major standalone frontier AI lab to go public.

According to the report, demand has been driven by indications of interest big enough to anchor the deal. In other words, individual investors are signalling orders large enough to underpin the whole book.

A filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on Tuesday set the price range at $70 to $78 a share, which would value the company at about $1.4 trillion. Anthropic is offering around 801 million Class A shares, and existing investors plan to sell roughly 24 million more. Separately, Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, Google, Micron Technology, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC have committed to buy a combined $26 billion of Class N common stock through a private placement.

Together, the IPO and placement target about $90 billion. That would beat SpaceX’s June debut, which raised $75 billion in its base offering and about $86 billion once its over-allotment option was exercised. On the filing’s numbers, though, the $90 billion total assumes pricing at the top of the range. It also includes shares sold by existing holders, and that money goes to them, not to the company. At the bottom of the range, the combined total would be closer to $84 billion, short of SpaceX’s full raise.

The valuation is also a sharp step up from the private market. In June, Anthropic raised $65 billion at a $965 billion valuation, a round investors described as heavily oversubscribed, before filing confidentially for its listing. A $1.4 trillion valuation would be roughly 45% above that level.

To keep momentum going, chief executive Dario Amodei will hold a live-streamed event with JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon on Friday, the report said.

Final pricing will be the first real test of what public investors will pay for a frontier AI developer itself, not just the chipmakers and cloud providers that supply it. Seven of those suppliers are now also shareholders through the placement, which ties their fortunes more closely to Anthropic’s. Whether the deal prices at the top of the range, or gets bigger, will show how much of the private-market enthusiasm carries over. 

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: Economic and event calendar in Asia Thursday, November 12, 2026 - low impact
item.description:
Its a low key day for the data agenda. The PPI data from Japan is of interest. 

Japan’s October producer price index (the corporate goods price index) is due at 23:50 GMT (18:50 US Eastern). Consensus looks for prices to rise 0.3% on the month, reversing September’s 0.3% drop. The annual rate is expected at 6.5%, down from 6.8%.

September’s figure missed forecasts. The annual rate slowed to 6.8% from 7.6% in August, mainly because of a 13.3% annual fall in agricultural prices as newly harvested rice got cheaper. An annual pace near 7% is still far above anything consistent with the BoJ’s price goal, though, so a softer October print would not mean pipeline pressure has gone away.

Three things to watch:

  1. Import prices. The yen-based import price index rose 24.5% year on year in September, or about 25%, with the weak yen still pushing up raw material costs. (Japan wholesale inflation misses at 6.8% but stays high enough to keep BOJ hike alive )
  2. Energy pass-through. Elevated oil prices linked to the Iran war magnify the effect of a weak yen on a country that imports most of its energy.
  3. Monthly momentum. If the month-on-month figure turns positive again, it would suggest the September dip was a blip and not the start of a turn lower.

BoJ implications

The BoJ held at 1.25% in an 8-1 vote on October 30, with Takata dissenting in favour of a hike to 1.5%. The board also raised its FY2027 inflation forecast to 2.6% from 2.4%. In a Bloomberg survey, 83% of economists expect the next hike in December, up from 35% a month earlier. The next policy meeting is on 17-18 December.

A print close to consensus is unlikely to change the December picture. A clear upside surprise would strengthen the hike case and could give the yen some support. A downside miss is unlikely to derail a hike, since the BoJ puts more weight on underlying consumer inflation and wages than on upstream goods prices.

This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

item.title: US stocks rally as AI shares rebound
item.description:
US stocks closed higher on Wednesday, with AI infrastructure and semiconductor shares leading the recovery. The Nasdaq 100 rose 2.28%, followed by a 1.60% gain in the Nasdaq Composite. The Dow participated, but its 0.48% advance lagged the broader indices.

CoreWeave helped give buyers a reason to step back into the AI trade. Stronger revenue, higher guidance and management’s plans to address funding concerns eased some of the anxiety surrounding the company’s expansion. That encouraged buying across related shares, although the longer-term financing and profitability questions remain.

The rally also had participation behind it. Advancers outnumbered decliners across every group in the supplied breadth snapshot. However, the Mag 7 remained divided, with Microsoft, Meta and Amazon finishing lower.

AI infrastructure and chip shares lead the buying

The standout gains came from companies tied to AI computing capacity, memory, chip design and data-center connectivity. These were substantial moves, with all seven names below posting double-digit percentage gains:

The buying reached beyond the largest technology companies. Cloud infrastructure providers, memory suppliers, optical connectivity companies and power-related shares all featured among the winners. That gave the recovery more depth.

  • Meta: −$12.62 (−1.97%) to $628.77.

  • Microsoft: −$12.03 (−2.26%) to $521.13.

The Nasdaq 100’s strong gain despite those three declining heavyweights highlights the strength elsewhere in the index. Buyers were making a play across a wider group of technology shares.

Market breadth supports the advance

The breadth of the market showed a positive split.

  • Dow: 18 advancing; 12 declining.

  • S&P 500: 311 advancing; 174 declining.

  • Nasdaq 100: 83 advancing; 17 declining.

  • Nasdaq: 1,933 advancing; 1,275 declining.

  • NYSE Composite: 1,030 advancing; 754 declining.

The Nasdaq 100 had the strongest participation, with nearly five advancing issues for every declining issue. Broader Nasdaq and NYSE breadth was positive, but less decisive. That points to a rally with widespread participation and a particularly strong concentration in large technology shares.

What traders can learn from today’s rally

An index gain tells you the direction. Breadth helps tell you how many stocks are participating.

Today, the Nasdaq 100 had both a strong percentage gain and strong participation. That is encouraging for buyers. But a sharp rebound alone does not establish a lasting change in trend. The next step is follow-through: buyers need to defend the recovery and continue making progress through resistance.

For individual stocks, the index is a useful barometer, but each stock still needs its own bias, risk and targets. Microsoft, Meta and Amazon were reminders of that today.

  • US VP Vance is considering face-to-face talks with a top Iranian security official as he emerges as the lead negotiator with Iran, in an effort to end a war seen as a drag on the Republican Party.

Analysis:

The key here is the reported backing from Trump. Giving Vance authority to negotiate could create an opening for more direct discussions. However, “considering” and “preliminary” remain the important qualifiers. There is no confirmed meeting or agreement in the supplied report.

For traders, credible progress toward ending the war would potentially weigh on crude oil’s geopolitical risk premium and support broader risk appetite. The next barometer is whether Iran agrees to meet and whether those discussions produce concrete commitments. The headline opens the door. Follow-through will determine how much confidence markets can put behind it.

Are Kushner and Steve Witkoff?

I wouldn’t call Kushner and Steve Witkoff “out” yet. The WSJ reports that Vance has become more active on Iran than the two envoys, who are also handling Russia–Ukraine negotiations. That points to a shift in responsibility, without confirming their removal.

My read is that Trump is putting more political weight behind the Iran channel. A vice president with authority to negotiate could give Tehran more confidence that proposals have direct White House backing. It also puts more responsibility on Vance to deliver.  Remember Vance blamed the Republican election defeat on the war. It would not be out of the ordinary for Trump to therefore say, "Well if that what you think, you go get a peace deal".   If Vance gets one, Trump takes credit. If he can't Vance gets the blame.  

For the post, I’d frame it this way: “Vance’s emergence suggests a shift in who is driving the negotiations. Elevating the talks to the vice-presidential level could help move difficult decisions forward, but a change in negotiator alone does not mean the two sides are closer to an agreement.”

item.title: U.S. asks Russia for new European security proposal as Ukraine talks regain momentum
item.description:
Axios is reporting: 

  • The U.S. has asked Russia to submit a new European security proposal that includes both Moscow’s demands and steps it would take to ease tensions with Europe.
  • Russia has long sought limits on NATO expansion and a reduced military presence in Eastern Europe. The request opens the door to discussions, but does not mean Washington has accepted those demands.
  • Trump envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are scheduled to meet Putin on Thursday, followed by a meeting with Zelensky in Dublin.
  • The U.S. also wants European representatives included in future peace talks. Russia continues to resist their participation.
  • The Abu Dhabi talks produced a prisoner-exchange agreement that could be the largest since the war began. The final number remains subject to discussions with the leaders.
  • Washington wants to negotiate a Ukraine peace deal and a broader European security arrangement simultaneously, with the security agreement implemented after a deal to end the war.
  • Europe remains a major hurdle. Ursula von der Leyen says discussions on a new security framework should come after the war ends. According to Axios, Washington has told allies that any agreement requires European and Ukrainian support and would not give Russia a veto over European security.

SUMMARY:

The U.S. is looking to broaden the Ukraine peace negotiations, asking Russia to put a new European security proposal on the table. According to Axios, the request comes with a condition: Moscow needs to outline what it is prepared to do to reduce tensions and reassure Europe, alongside its own security demands. That opens the door to a wider negotiation, but there is still plenty of work to do before the two sides can move toward an agreement.

There has been some progress. The Abu Dhabi talks produced a potentially significant prisoner-exchange agreement, and Witkoff and Kushner are set to take the next round of discussions directly to Putin and Zelensky on Thursday. However, European participation remains a sticking point. Washington wants Europe at the table. Russia continues to push back, while European governments remain deeply skeptical of the broader security proposal.

The sequencing is another key hurdle. Washington wants the peace deal and security framework negotiated together. Von der Leyen wants the war ended before discussing a new security architecture. For markets, my takeaway is that the diplomatic door is opening a little wider, but the next barometer is whether Russia offers concrete concessions and accepts European participation. That would give the optimism a firmer foundation. Until then, this remains progress toward negotiations, with the difficult decisions still ahead.

item.title: BOE’s Greene: Appropriate to proactively tighten policy against wage risks
item.description:
BOE’s Greene said monetary policy should lean against the risk of wage growth becoming entrenched at higher levels, according to the FT.

  • It is appropriate to proactively tighten our monetary policy stance to lean against the risk of wage growth getting stuck at higher levels.

Other BOE comments this week

Governor Bailey highlighted the potential benefits of AI investment:

  • In the UK, economic activity is turning out to be more resilient than we had expected, and some of that is due to AI investment, particularly in the business services sector.

  • We are seeing growing signs of the beginnings of a positive supply shock coming from AI and the investment required for that.

Deputy Governor Lombardelli kept a December hike on the table, according to the Guardian:

  • A further 25bps rate hike in December is plausible, with every meeting live, but a decision will depend on developments in the Iran conflict.

Breeden commented on businesses’ response to higher costs:

  • Firms are now very good at adapting to cost shocks.

Lombardelli also warned about persistent inflation and problems beneath the surface of the labour market:

  • In setting monetary policy, will continue to look beyond the headline numbers: at whether hiring is recovering, whether people can move towards the jobs available, and whether labour market weakness is genuinely easing wage and inflation pressures. That evidence will shape judgement of how much further monetary policy needs to go to return inflation sustainably to the 2% target.

  • Argues that the conditions for persistent inflationary dynamics over the mid-term are crystallizing.

  • The longer energy costs stay high, the greater the pressure there will be on businesses to restore margins.

  • Energy shock has become more persistent.

  • Greater prospect of second-round effects.

  • Balance of inflation risks to the upside.

  • The labour market is stuck in low gear; UK has a low-hire, low-fire labour market that creates its own problems; might be necessary to raise rates further in the near term.

On economic resilience and spare capacity, Lombardelli added:

  • Policy has been less restrictive than thought, due to economic resilience.

  • Hard to determine if the UK economy is more resilient to price shocks, or if the absorption limit is being approached.

  • Thinks there could be less slack in the UK economy vs the BOE’s central view, at 0–1% vs 1%.

Analysis:

Greene’s message is hawkish. She favors getting ahead of the risk that wage growth gets stuck at levels that keep inflation elevated. The key word is “proactively.” That suggests a willingness to tighten before the persistence becomes fully established. Lombardelli’s comments lean in the same direction. A weak hiring backdrop does not automatically mean wage pressures are easing, particularly if workers cannot move easily into the jobs available. If the economy also has less spare capacity than the BOE assumes, there is less room for demand to grow without adding to inflation.

For traders, the comments keep the risk of another hike firmly in play, with December a live possibility rather than a commitment. Bailey’s AI comments offer a potentially more favorable supply story over time, but stronger investment also helps explain why activity has held up. The barometer going forward is whether wage growth and business pricing pressures actually ease. A sustained decline in energy costs would help, but if businesses continue passing through earlier cost increases and wages remain sticky, the argument for further tightening stays intact.

item.title: CoreWeave surges after earnings. Can buyers turn the rebound into something more?
item.description:
CoreWeave shares are sharply higher after earnings, giving buyers some relief after a punishing decline. From the June 2025 high near $187, the price tumbled to $40.58 on November 5. That represented a decline of roughly 78%. Today, the shares are up around 25% and trading near $61.25.

For those unfamiliar with the company, CoreWeave provides cloud computing infrastructure designed for artificial intelligence. It operates data centers equipped with powerful Nvidia processors, renting computing capacity to companies building and running AI models. That puts CoreWeave directly in the middle of the AI infrastructure spending story. It also makes the company heavily dependent on financing the equipment and capacity needed to meet that demand.

That financing requirement has been a major part of the recent bearish storyline. Investors have questioned whether future AI revenue can justify the enormous spending taking place today. CoreWeave’s heavy debt burden, rising bond yields and concerns about the cost of funding its expansion made the shares particularly vulnerable as sentiment toward the AI trade deteriorated.

The latest earnings give buyers something to work with.

Third-quarter revenue rose 168% from a year earlier to $3.66 billion, above the roughly $3.54 billion expected by analysts. Adjusted operating income reached $379 million, with an adjusted operating margin of 10%. Management said that double-digit margin arrived a quarter ahead of plan. The revenue backlog stood at approximately $132.5 billion, although converting that backlog into revenue requires the company to deliver the contracted services.

However, the company remains loss-making. The quarterly GAAP net loss widened to $709 million, or $1.27 per share, while net interest expense reached $846 million. Revenue growth is strong, but the cost of financing that growth remains a key part of the equation.

The forward guidance provided another reason for buyers to step in:

  • Full-year revenue guidance increased to $13.0 billion–$13.3 billion, from $12.4 billion–$13.2 billion.

  • Adjusted operating income guidance increased to $1.275 billion–$1.375 billion, a 26% increase at the midpoint.

  • The year-end annualized revenue run rate is now expected to reach $20 billion–$21 billion. That measures the final month’s revenue multiplied by 12.

  • Capital spending is expected to total $37 billion–$39 billion, with the lower end raised from $35 billion as infrastructure comes online sooner.

Management also addressed the funding concerns directly. It expects approximately $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits over the next three months and said it does not intend to issue additional parent-level unsecured debt at current yields through 2027. The company expects adjusted losses to narrow meaningfully next year, with positive adjusted net income targeted for the first half of 2028 and the full year. Those are management’s expectations, but they help explain why buyers are reassessing the recent selling.

From a technical perspective, buyers have taken a step forward.

Looking at the hourly chart, the October rally stalled near $93.14, where the 100 and 200 day moving averages were in play. Buyers had their shot to take back control above those longer-term barometers. They could not sustain the break, sellers leaned against the area, and the price subsequently tumbled to $40.58.

Today’s earnings rebound has pushed the price back above the 100 hour moving average, shown near $53.38 on the chart. More immediately, it has also reclaimed the end-of-July low at $60.55.

That $60.55 level now becomes the close risk level for buyers.

With the shares trading near $61.25, buyers will want to hold above that old low and build acceptance above it. Stay above, and the next key target is the falling 200 hour moving average at $64.34. That is where buyers face their next test. Moving above the 100 hour moving average improved the short-term picture. Getting above the 200 hour moving average would give buyers more control.

A break above $64.34 would open the door toward the 38.2% retracement of the decline from the August high at $69.90. Above that, the 50% midpoint at $78.96 and the falling 100 day moving average near $80.17 form another important target area.

Conversely, a move back below $60.55 would take some of the momentum out of today’s break and raise the risk of a rotation back toward the 100 hour moving average at $53.39.

The earnings have provided the catalyst. Now buyers need to follow through. Hold above $60.55 and break the 200 hour moving average, and the recovery has room to extend. Lose $60.55, and sellers have an opening to challenge the rebound.

About CoreWeave

CoreWeave is a cloud computing company built specifically for artificial intelligence. It operates data centers filled with powerful Nvidia processors and rents that computing capacity to businesses that need to train AI models and run AI applications. Customers gain access to expensive computing infrastructure without having to build and operate it themselves. Its customers include Microsoft and OpenAI.

The company combines that hardware with software and technical support to help customers manage demanding AI workloads. Its growth depends on bringing additional computing capacity online and turning customer commitments into revenue. CoreWeave reported approximately $132.5 billion in revenue backlog at the end of September, subject to delivery and service requirements. investors.coreweave.com

The opportunity is substantial, but so is the cost. CoreWeave must fund processors, data centers and power before collecting much of the associated revenue. That makes access to financing, interest costs and the pace of AI demand central to its business—and helps explain why its shares can be particularly sensitive to concerns about AI spending.

item.title: Iran’s Ghalibaf: Peace is our priority if Washington accepts our conditions
item.description:
Iranian Parliament Speaker and head of the negotiating delegation Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf spoke to Al Jazeera about negotiations with Washington, the Strait of Hormuz and the risk of further conflict:

We have reached an understanding with #عمان on the shipping lane and traffic separation scheme in the Strait of Hormuz

  • Our priority is peace if they accept our conditions, and we do not want the war to continue.

  • Continuing the war will harm the countries of the region, their security and their economies.

  • The Americans visited Moscow and asked Putin to speak with Iran to arrange direct negotiations between us.

  • If Trump decides to go to war again, he will face another defeat.

  • We are determined to move beyond the state of neither war nor peace, not necessarily through negotiations but through sustained deterrence.

  • Ending the war with Iran and the resistance front is one of the points in the memorandum of understanding and one of our seven conditions.

  • If America or Israel starts a war, we will confront them together and respond to any attack.

  • We have given America a clear and transparent response that includes our demands.

  • Washington has not yet provided an official and specific response to our letter.

  • Washington must meet our seven conditions to open the Strait of Hormuz and resume negotiations.

  • We have presented a clear and transparent response to America that includes our demands.

  • The ball is now in the Americans’ court, and they must make a decision and announce it.

The door to an agreement remains open, but the conditions remain firm. The rebound is giving buyers an opportunity. Now they need to hold the reclaimed support and work through the resistance above.

The trading lesson: Let the levels measure the recovery.

A strong percentage gain gets attention, but the technical levels help determine how much has changed.

For the Nasdaq indices, the reclaimed support areas define the risk. For the S&P 500, the immediate test is whether buyers can push through the swing area and moving averages overhead.

item.title: Crude oil faces a geopolitical test as Russia signals progress toward peace
item.description:
Russia’s top Ukraine negotiator, Vladimir Medinsky, says it appears the sides are moving closer to peace, although much still depends on all participants in the process. The headline offers some encouragement, but the qualification matters. Progress toward an agreement still requires the parties to turn that optimism into concrete commitments.

Following the talks in Abu Dhabi, Medinsky reported common ground on some issues and continued differences on others, with discussions set to continue. Russia and Ukraine also agreed to a large-scale prisoner exchange. Those are steps forward, but significant issues remain unresolved.

Peace hopes could weigh on oil’s risk premium.

For crude oil, the potential implication is a reduction in the premium traders pay for the risk of supply disruptions. A credible path toward peace could ease concerns about attacks on energy infrastructure and raise expectations for fewer restrictions on Russian oil flows over time.

That would be a potentially bearish development. However, a peace agreement would not automatically remove sanctions or immediately bring additional barrels to market. The terms of any agreement, the timing of implementation and the response from Western governments would all matter. Of course, there is also what is happening in the middle east.  That is also in play of course.

For now, the distinction is between hopes for a deal and an agreement that changes the supply outlook. Encouraging headlines can give sellers a reason to push. Sustained follow-through would require evidence that the underlying risks are actually easing.

The headlines provide the catalyst. The technicals define the risk.

The diplomatic headlines provide the catalyst, but the technical levels will help determine whether sellers can turn that optimism into a sustained move lower in crude oil. Can they break support and take control, or will buyers lean against that support and force a rotation back higher?

A cluster of technical levels defines the battle.

Looking at the 4-hour chart below, crude oil broke below its 100 and 200 day moving averages during Monday’s trade, along with the 50% midpoint of the move higher from the July low to the September high.

Today, buyers tried to reclaim that area. The price reached $87.56, briefly moving above the 100 day moving average, before the latest diplomatic headline helped send it back toward $87.00.

That leaves three closely grouped levels in play:

  • 100 day moving average at $87.47.

  • 200 day moving average at $87.34.

  • 50% midpoint at $86.93.

With the price trading within that cluster, buyers and sellers are still battling for control. The area is the near-term barometer for the next directional move.

Buyers need to hold above $87.47. Sellers need to break $86.93.

For buyers, getting above the 100 day moving average at $87.47—and staying above it—would put the price back above all three technical levels. That would strengthen the bullish bias and open the door for further upside momentum. Today’s push to $87.56 showed that buyers can get above the area. The missing ingredient is the ability to sustain the break.

Conversely, a move below the $86.93 midpoint with momentum would shift control back toward the sellers. Staying below that level would leave the full cluster overhead as resistance and bring Tuesday’s low near the natural support at $84.00 back into focus.

The risk is therefore well defined. Above $87.47, buyers have a stronger technical footing. Below $86.93, sellers have the advantage. Between those levels, the battle continues.

Meanwhile in the Middle East...

Meanwhile in the Middle East, the geopolitical risks are moving in the opposite direction. Iran’s Rezaei warned that US military bases in Europe would be targeted if American aircraft departed from those bases to strike Iran. For crude oil, that threat provides a counterweight to the optimism surrounding the Russia-Ukraine peace talks. Progress toward peace in Ukraine could help reduce oil’s risk premium, but the potential for a broader confrontation involving Iran could keep traders wary of supply disruptions. The threat alone does not change the physical supply picture, but it gives sellers another risk to consider as they try to push prices lower.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: The price of Bitcoin is little changed but off the support target. What next?
item.description:
Bitcoin finds buyers near key technical support.

Bitcoin fell yesterday to its lowest level since August 20. In the process, the price broke below its 200 day moving average, currently at $73,117, but stopped short of the 50% midpoint of the move up from the July 1 low to the September high.

That midpoint comes in at $72,554. Yesterday’s low reached $72,677, leaving the sellers just $123 short of that key target.

The subsequent bounce suggests buyers were willing to lean against the support area, with risk defined by a break below. The price has since recovered above the 200 day moving average and currently trades near $73,706, little changed on the day.

So what next?

Buyers remain in play, but have work to do.

The recovery above the 200 day moving average gives buyers a short-term foothold. However, holding support is only the first step. They now need to extend the recovery through resistance.

The next key target is the swing area between $74,925 and $76,052. That area was defined by a number of swing highs and lows going back to August 20. On Sunday, the price broke below it with more downside momentum and has remained below since.

If buyers are to take back more control, they need to get and stay above that area. Doing so would open the door toward the 100 day moving average near $77,621.

Until then, the bounce remains a correction into an area that was once support and is now resistance.

Sellers need to break the downside support.

For sellers, the roadmap starts with a move back below the 200 day moving average at $73,117. That would weaken the recovery and shift attention back toward yesterday’s low at $72,677, followed by the more important 50% midpoint at $72,554.

A break below the midpoint with momentum would give sellers more control and open the door toward the natural support at $70,000. Below that, the 61.8% retracement comes in at $69,057.

Those are the downside targets if the support buyers lose their foothold.

The battle lines are defined.

Buyers leaning against support want to see the price hold above the 200 day moving average and build momentum toward $74,925–$76,052. A sustained break above that resistance area would strengthen their case for a larger recovery.

Sellers want to keep that resistance ceiling intact and push the price back below the 200 day moving average and the $72,554 midpoint.

Between those areas, the battle continues. Support has attracted buyers, but the sellers still have a resistance area to lean against.

In the video above…

In the video above, I outline the support that helped stall Bitcoin’s decline, explain why the $74,925–$76,052 swing area is the next key upside test, and walk through the levels that would give buyers or sellers more control.

Education: A support bounce needs follow-through.

A bounce near a key technical level gives traders a place to define and limit risk. It does not, by itself, confirm that the broader direction has changed.

The next test is how the price behaves at resistance. If buyers can break above former support and stay above it, they add credibility to the recovery. If the rally stalls there, sellers can lean against that same area and look for another rotation lower.

For Bitcoin, the support levels define the buyers’ risk. The $74,925–$76,052 resistance area tests whether they can turn a defensive bounce into a stronger recovery.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: Morning Kickstart: AI stocks rebound as USD after hot CPI. Thank you Veterans for your service
item.description:
Stocks are bouncing this morning. The inflation problem is still there.

CoreWeave’s earnings have given buyers a reason to move back into beaten-down AI and semiconductor shares, with Nasdaq 100 futures leading the recovery. At the same time, the U.S. dollar is higher across the major currencies after yesterday’s hotter-than-expected CPI report and another round of hawkish Fed commentary.

That leaves traders balancing two different stories. The AI spending outlook is offering some reassurance for technology stocks. The inflation and interest-rate outlook is offering considerably less reassurance for the broader economy.

In the morning video above, I take a look at the three major currency pairs—EURUSD, USDJPY and GBPUSD—from a technical perspective. For each pair, I outline the bias, the risk-defining levels and the targets that would give either the buyers or sellers more control.

CPI keeps the pressure on the Fed

Yesterday’s CPI report was disturbing because the underlying inflation picture failed to improve as much as hoped. Headline prices rose 0.4% versus 0.3% expected, while core prices increased 0.3% versus 0.2% expected. It was the third consecutive rounded monthly core reading of 0.3%.

Energy inflation slowed from September, but that did not produce a corresponding slowdown in core inflation. Shelter and other service prices remained part of the problem. My Americas FX wrap from yesterday reviews the report and the market reaction.

The message from Fed officials is becoming harder to ignore:

  • Christopher Waller, Federal Reserve governor: A 50-basis-point increase is on the table. His comments before CPI tied consideration of a larger move to another core reading of 0.3% or higher.

  • Lorie Logan, Dallas Fed president: At least two more quarter-point increases are needed, with scope to move more quickly.

  • Austan Goolsbee, Chicago Fed president: Inflation is “borderline disturbing,” with service inflation failing to come down.

  • Anna Paulson, Philadelphia Fed president: Further gradual increases are appropriate, but a worsening inflation outlook could require more aggressive action. She sees a stronger-than-expected economy and a robust, stable labor market.

  • Michelle Bowman, Federal Reserve governor: Inflation’s failure to trend lower should give policymakers pause. The question is what pace and timeline are needed to address it.

My read is that the debate is shifting toward how quickly the Fed needs to tighten further. A half-point increase is a possibility, not a decision. But it gives traders another risk to account for. The market is pricing in a 13% chance for a 50 BP hike.  

Treasury market closed after a sharp repricing

The U.S. cash Treasury market is closed today for Veterans Day. Yesterday’s levels therefore provide the reference point:

  • 2-year Treasury yield: Rose around 20 basis points.

  • 10-year Treasury yield: Closed at 5.00%, compared with a low of 4.817% last Thursday.

That is an approximately 18.3-basis-point climb in the 10-year yield from Thursday’s low.

The 2-year move is particularly relevant to the Fed outlook because that maturity is sensitive to expectations for short-term policy rates. The 10-year matters more broadly for mortgages, corporate borrowing and equity valuations.

Today’s stock rebound will have to wait until tomorrow for the next full cash Treasury-market response. The holiday does not remove the interest-rate headwind.

Nvidia rebounded about 4.4% following two sharply lower sessions, while Micron and Marvell also advanced. The concentration of gains in AI and semiconductor shares helps explain why the Nasdaq is outperforming the Dow.

My read: buyers have found a reason to step back in after the selling. That is encouraging for the AI trade, but one earnings report does not resolve the tension between strong investment demand and a higher cost of financing.

The next test is whether the gains hold once regular trading gets underway.

Dollar higher across the board

The dollar is stronger against every major currency in the supplied snapshot. Its largest gain is against the Swiss franc, while the Australian dollar is holding up best with only a modest decline against the greenback.

The dollar’s ability to hold its gains while technology shares rebound is worth watching. So far, improved equity sentiment has not been enough to reverse the currency market’s response to inflation and the Fed.

Currency ranges: Room remains to extend

Using the displayed session highs and lows and the 22-day average ranges:

  • EURUSD: 1.1131–1.1170 — 39 pips, approximately 57% of its 68-pip average.

  • GBPUSD: 1.3308–1.3358 — 50 pips, approximately 64% of its 78-pip average.

AUDUSD has completed the smallest share of its normal range. USDCHF has used the most, although it remains below its average.

There is still room for an extension in the major pairs if prices break their session extremes. The averages provide context; they do not require prices to travel farther or prevent them from exceeding a normal day’s range.

Crude rebounds as diplomacy faces obstacles

At approximately 7:25 AM ET, WTI crude oil was trading at $87.28, up $1.24, or 1.44%. The session range was $85.81–$87.39, leaving the price near its high.

The Middle East remains central to the outlook. Qatar said it had secured at least two weeks for diplomatic efforts between the U.S. and Iran, but significant differences remain. Iranian officials have also pushed back against reports of negotiations and concessions.

As InvestingLive’s oil update explains, the absence of a concrete breakthrough is challenging expectations for a quick agreement. That provides a backdrop for today’s rebound.

On Russia and Ukraine, trilateral talks involving the U.S. have concluded, with further updates awaited on whether substantive progress was made. The talks keep diplomacy in focus, but they do not yet establish a settlement or a change in energy supply.

The next inflation release highlighted on the calendar is U.S. PPI on Friday, November 13, at 8:30 AM ET. After yesterday’s CPI surprise, traders will look for evidence of persistent pipeline price pressures and details that could influence estimates for the Fed’s preferred PCE inflation measure.

Good fortune with your trading.

Crude oil has been edging higher recently amid the lack of concrete breakthrough in US-Iran negotiations.

Qatar said yesterday that it secured at least two weeks for diplomatic efforts, adding that significant differences remain. So, the expectations for an imminent deal should be repriced and that will likely lead to a rebound in oil prices.

Crude oil fell significantly following the US midterm elections on the wrong assumptions that the Republicans’ loss would force Trump to wrap up the Iran war quickly. The reality is that Trump can continue the war without Congress. Moreover, it’s not even logical to leave now that he doesn’t have anything to lose.

We can argue that the midterm loss has made things even worse for negotiations as Iran got emboldened by the Democrats victory. Tehran continues to insist on their terms, but the US has never considered those acceptable. So, the stalemate could drag on more than expected and Trump could also consider limited strikes against nuclear facilities rather than broader attacks on energy infrastructure.

It goes without saying that a concrete breakthrough would trigger a significant selloff and take oil prices back to pre-war levels relatively quickly. But an escalation, on the other hand, could trigger another rally on a rising risk premium, although there’s also a chance that it could be short-lived if Trump launches limited strikes just to save face before exiting the war.

item.title: USD/JPY knocks on the door of 159.00 again, dollar bulls risk poking the intervention bear

Well, well, well. It looks like dollar bulls are knocking on the door again in search of a break higher in USD/JPY. But if they manage to kick the door open this time, they might just find Japanese authorities waiting on the other side of it.

USD/JPY is trading up to seven-week highs today, clipping 159.00 as buyers attempt to break through a resistance region that has frustrated them for quite a few weeks now.

The previous attempts to push to the upside were capped by resistance at the 200-day moving average (blue line), with the swing region around 159.00 providing an added layer to that. But today, USD/JPY buyers are looking to prove their worth as they try to tackle both key levels at one go. At the same time though, they need to wrestle with the 100-day moving average (red line) at 158.98 currently too.

For now, buyers will have to really take a bold step in challenging that confluence and making a daily close above it in order to confirm an upside breakout. A firm break above the key technical levels above would take the pair to its highest levels in over two months, with 160.00 emerging as the next key psychological target.

Looking at what's driving the move, the dollar certainly has some fundamental backing. The hotter-than-expected US CPI report yesterday and more hawkish Fed commentary have strengthened expectations of further rate hikes, providing an impetus for the greenback while the yen continues to meander amid a lack of hawkish conviction from the BOJ itself.

That being said, what's curious is that the dollar is holding firmer despite the broader improvement in risk sentiment so far today. Equities are seen rebounding with tech shares surging higher and Wall Street is looking poised to recover the drop from yesterday. But with the US bond market closed for Veterans Day, traders aren't getting any fresh signals from Treasury yields to validate the move.

As such, this is where things get a bit tricky.

And when you throw in the fact that the closer USD/JPY gets to 160.00, the more uncomfortable the long trade becomes. Tokyo officials are definitely watching this space closely and Japan's sizeable interventions earlier this year are a reminder that they aren't afraid to act against excessive yen weakness.

This is not to say that 160.00 is going to be a magic intervention trigger point in which Japan authorities will act, but any rapid move higher could invite stronger verbal warnings or even direct action if need be from hereon.

All in all, that leaves dollar bulls facing an awkward dilemma. The technicals are looking good again with some encouragement to break to the upside. However, just the very threat of Japanese intervention alone may make buyers extremely reluctant to chase the move. Tough.

This article was written by Justin Low at investinglive.com.

item.title: Ethereum extends losses as Fed's Waller puts a larger rate hike on the table and US CPI remains hot
item.description:
Ethereum came under pressure yesterday as Fed's Waller surprised markets with some very hawkish remarks in his speech on the economic outlook.

He suggested that a rate hike in December would be warranted regardless of yesterday's inflation data, adding that the only thing the data would influence would be the magnitude of the increase. In fact, he said that a Core CPI M/M reading of 0.3% or higher would lead him to vote for a larger 50 bps hike.

His remarks led to a hawkish repricing, sending Treasury yields and the US dollar higher. This weighed on risk sentiment, putting downward pressure on Ethereum.

The Core CPI then came in at 0.3%, sending Treasury yields and the US dollar even higher as expectations of a potentially larger rate hike increased.

Meanwhile, nothing has changed on the US-Iran front. Qatar said yesterday that it had secured at least two weeks for diplomatic efforts, while acknowledging that significant differences remain. This suggests that expectations for an imminent deal may need to be repriced, potentially leading to a rebound in oil prices and a more negative risk sentiment.

For now, the macro backdrop remains negative for Ethereum, unless we get a concrete breakthrough in US-Iran negotiations or a more dovish Fed.

If we get a pullback, we can expect the sellers to lean on the trendline, with a defined risk above it, to keep targeting the 1,900 level. The buyers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking higher to extend the pullback into the major downward trendline.
